system.effect:
Dynamax is a type of special physical transformation Pokémon can undergo, warping the space around them to change their size and affect the world around them, using the incredible power stored within a Wishing Star. Two prerequisites must be met before Dynamax can be applied, however. First, the Trainer must be wearing an Accessory Slot item containing a Wishing Star. Second, the Wishing Star must have accumulated enough energy to engage in the process.

Dynamax can be initiated on the Trainer’s turn as a Standard Action. Once triggered, Dyanmax lasts for 3 rounds while the Pokémon is on the field. A Dynamax Band can only power one Dynamax until it recharges, meaning once a Trainer Dynamaxes a Pokémon, they can’t Dynamax any others until the Dynamax Band is recharged.

Note: If a Trainer is incapacitated before the Dynamax activation completely resolves, the Wishing Star’s charge is not expended and the target isn’t Dynamaxed, but the Trainer still uses their Standard Action.

When a Pokémon Dynamaxes, place Blast 6 with the user in one of the center 4 squares. Any other creatures within the Blast are then pushed to the nearest unoccupied space outside
of the Blast. The user then increases its space to fill the Blast that was placed, growing to D-Max Size, and gains Temporary Hit Points equal to its current Hit Point maximum. 

If the user would not be able to fit in the space around it at the end of this transformation, the user either shapes the area around it so it can occupy the space (often destroying objects and terrain), or is forcefully moved to a space it can safely occupy. This is done at the discretion of the GM.

Dynamaxed Pokémon receive +3 to each of their Movement Capabilities and receive the Mountable 4 Capability. Those Pokémon that already had Mountable have their Mountable Rating increase by +4. Dynamaxed Pokémon cannot be forcefully recalled by anything other than their own Moves, Abilities, Capabilities, held items, actions, or those of their Trainer.

Some Pokemon have access to a special type of Dynamax, called Gigantamax. While they do have vastly different appearances compared to their original Forme, they function identically to standard Dynamax, with the only difference being in their possible access to different Moves.

Note: In the Galar Region, Dynamax may only be initiated while at a Power Spot, which are areas that contain vast quantities of ambient energy that, when catalyzed by a Wishing Star, allow for the Pokémon to Dynamax. GMs are strongly advised to have restrictions in place for their settings for allowing/disallowing Dynamaxing and managing the recharges as the raw capabilities and kaiju-like proportions of Dynamaxed Pokémon can be an issue both in terms of gameplay and narrative.
